ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with onset in early childhood, characterized by asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules and severe skin sagging, primarily affecting flexural areas
salient_findings: Yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules developed in early childhood
Skin sagging occurred on the abdomen and spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis on skin biopsy
Compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
